title: Baseball in New Orleans and the Negro league teams
summary: The interviewer and Albert discuss New Orleans ballparks and the visiting Negro league teams Albert watched as a boy.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I'm interested in baseball a little bit. I don't know much about it, but you do. I've always been fascinated in talking to people. Like, I don't know if you know Mooney Martin or not, but he used to play baseball long before your time and he's a friend of Tom Albers, but he would tell me about the different teams, Algiers they had, and they had teams out in the country. You know, and I hear different people talk about that. Well, New Orleans was a big baseball

town and I used to go to the old Crescent Star Park, which was back in town, as you used to say, and went on the outside for a foul ball to come over and scramble with the other kids and get the ball and go in. What was the first time? Somewhere in back town. I can't remember the exact location. Look it up. And I'm sure some of the more at least can pin-pink the question so far. What about the Dixie Park? I don't know anything about the Dixie Park.

See, I have old posters that John Robichoke said, you know, that you wouldn't even remember the places of the team. Now, I don't know whether they, you know, at that time, but I don't know if they lasted on into your time. John Robichoke said he'd say things for years and years. Anyway, Dixie Park, I've seen about Lincoln and Johnson Park and Oleander Park. Those were uptown folks. Yeah, those would be three uptown folks. No, I didn't go up there. Or Carrollton, as they would say. Carrollton, that's right. I didn't know.
All of them was that I knew was the Pelican, the Pelican Stadium. Did you play that? They got mostly the white teams.
And you went and watched them? Oh, no. I was too young. Would they let you into the white teams?
Well, the way they would is that they wouldn't question who I was.
I never have known. I know they had a team at one time called the Black Pelicans.

Well, that's why they named it. The Black Pelicans only called the Pelicans. Did you ever play with them? I never played. I was a boy. I was about eight, nine, eight or ten years old, possibly. You saw the Black Pelicans? Yes. I used to go to the Pelican, there's many catches, and sometimes the names come back to me. And Satchel Paige was down many times. And the team from Chicago, the Chicago Giants, used to take the players from the Orleans. They had one name. Jumbo Jackson was a great player baseman. And Hot Pocket was the first baseman. The Baccarat Giants, they played down there. Memphis Black Sox, or just any team that was on the Negro circuit. Came down there. And of course, the New Orleans always had a tremendous team. Had a left-handed killer than me.
And who else? You never saw Shooters Joe Jackson.
He's the one that's, you remember in 1990, when the White Sox had all that problem?
Right. But Shooters Joe Jackson was a white player.

Yeah, he was down there with the Pelicans. Well, yes, with the white Pelicans. The white Pelicans. Sure. So, but that other Jackson. Jumbo Jackson. There was another guy in town. So, they had a lot of teams coming in.

A lot of teams, a lot of great ball players. If they were living today, or if they could have captured them in those days. Josh Gibson was there. Satchel Caves. And all the other great ball players, Narco, N-R-P-E-L-B. And most of them used to go with the Giants.
